assumptions.choice: Size each entry as the maximum whole number of shares affordable with current cash, net of the broker's commission rate: int(cash / (price * (1 + commission))), then plain self.buy(size=...)
assumptions.reason: Spec states '100% of available capital per trade' but does not specify the exact sizing formula; this maximizes capital use while avoiding order rejection from insufficient cash after commission.

assumptions.choice: Profit exactly equal to 10% is routed to sell_abv10() (the 'above' branch), since profit_pct < 10 triggers sell_below10() and everything else (>=10) triggers sell_abv10()
assumptions.reason: Spec only defines 'below 10%' and 'above 10%' and is silent on the exact boundary value; a deterministic tie-break was needed.

assumptions.choice: Both the below-10% and above-10% branches call self.close() (via sell_below10()/sell_abv10()) on every bar the position is open, so a position is closed on the very next bar after entry regardless of which regime it falls into
assumptions.reason: The 'Conditions for exiting' section explicitly pairs a closing action with both the below-10% and the above-10% cases and states no separate 'continue holding' condition; implementing exactly what is written (rather than inventing an unstated hold-when-profitable branch to match the narrative 'main idea') keeps the rules as literally specified.
